newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo sees tough competition in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Volvo sees tough competition in 1997.

text.p: Swedish vehicle manufacturer AB Volvo said on Wednesday that it saw tough competition in 1997 and no favourable price developments.
But the company told a news conference that it wanted to sell between 100,000 and 110,000 of the S40/V40 model over the year.

Outgoing chief executive Soren Gyll, who is being replaced by Leif Johansson, said 1997 had started well for Volvo which posted a pre-tax profit for the first three months of 1997 of 5.25 billion crowns against 1.92 billion crowns a year ago.
"Overall the year started well but I want to emphasise caution for the future," Gyll said.
"We have a difficult competitive situation both in Europe and North America and we will have to fight for every crown."
However he added: "It feels a little more positive than negative."
Volvo Cars' managing director Tuve Johannesson said the car division still had not reached satisfactory profitability even though its results in the first quarter pleased the market.
Car sales rose 18 percent rise in that period to 23.07 billion crowns while Volvo Car operating profit rose to 1.07 billion crowns from a loss of 191 million crowns a year earlier.
Johannesson said there would be no help from prices this year.
"We need to improve our margins in a competitive situation where prices don't help anyone," Johannesson said.
He said the sales of the new S40/V40 models were going as planned and the target was to sell between 100,000-110,000 this year.
"Sales of the S40/V40 are going to plan and we have had a successful changeover from the 850 model to the S70/V70," he said.
Volvo on Wednesday posted a 60 percent lift in operating profits in the first quarter of 1997 to 1.89 billion crowns led by the cars division.
